extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO OED staff, legal counsel, and respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO final order imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state disbarment and setting related procedural requirements (notice, publication, reinstatement, dissociation from Customer Numbers/PKI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline may file a Complaint requesting that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a State disciplinary authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 must be mailed (certified mail evidence recorded). The Notice provided an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for exclusion: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO may be ordered for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) as predicate for disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order explicitly states exclusion is ordered for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon being disbarred on consent from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40 days) by certified mail
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order was mailed by certified mail and delivered to the Respondent, providing a 40-day period to respond opposing reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified mail receipt may be used to demonstrate delivery. Failure to file a response within the 40-day window is material to the procedural disposition (see No Genuine Issue entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: No genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, it may be determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such circumstances, the Office may conclude reciprocal discipline identical to the state sanction is appropriate without further factual hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary sanction: exclusion from practice before the USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark and other non-patent law before the USPTO effective on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exclusion mirrors the sanction imposed by the State (Illinois) and is applied to patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to seek reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with the sanction imposed by the State, the Respondent is granted the right to file a petition seeking reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 after serving three years of exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order ties USPTO reinstatement timing to the state rule (Supreme Court of Illinois Rule 767(a)), noting an attorney disbarred on consent may petition for reinstatement no earlier than three years after the disbarment-on-consent order date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the Exclusion, the factual basis (misconduct), the regulation violated, and reinstatement rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order includes the exact Notice text to be published, which identifies the respondent, registration number, predicate violation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), description of the state sanction, factual misconduct (criminal conspiracy/money laundering via client trust account), and reinstatement timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and reasons therefor to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the Respondent is admitted, to courts where the Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures reciprocal discipline is communicated to relevant jurisdictions and public bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of excluded practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded from practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the order does not restate § 11.58 duties, it mandates compliance (e.g., client notification/transfer obligations, restrictions on practice) as required by that regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an administrative action to prevent excluded practitioners from continuing to represent or file via USPTO electronic systems using prior credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to USPTO Customer Numbers until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, obtain a USPTO Customer Number, or have his name added to a USPTO Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction remains in place for the duration of the exclusion and until formal reinstatement under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of misconduct supporting state disbarment (Rule 8.4 violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state tribunal found Respondent engaged in criminal acts reflecting adversely on honesty, trustworthiness or fitness as a lawyer (Rule 8.4(a)(3)) and conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (Rule 8.4(a)(5)), specifically conspiring to commit federal crimes (money laundering) in violation of 18 U.S.C. § 371.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal convictions or conduct involving misuse of client trust accounts and conspiracies to launder funds can constitute professional misconduct warranting disbarment and reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of disciplinary decisions at OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are available for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order provides the URL (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) as the repository for published disciplinary decisions.
